Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real. But one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless. To counter that, Blue […]
article.author: Terrence O’Brien

post.caption:
When perfection starts looking fake, the only way to prove reality is leaving in the flaws.

For years, the BBC's Blue Planet franchise set the standard with immaculate, crystal-clear wildlife shots that looked almost impossibly pristine. But generative AI has flipped that dynamic on its head. Today, hyper-polished, seamless footage is often the biggest giveaway that a video was artificially generated.

To prove its authenticity, Blue Planet III is taking a deliberate counter-strategy: leaving less-than-perfect shots in the final cut. In the age of AI, organic roughness might be the strongest proof of reality.

#artificialintelligence #generativeai #blueplanet #naturedocumentary #techtrends #filmmaking #authenticity

📰 Source: AI | The Verge (by Terrence O’Brien) - https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1018205/blue-planet-iii-authentic-organic-ai
post.headline: Why Blue Planet III Is Embracing Imperfect Footage
slides_text: Why Blue Planet is embracing flaws
slides_body: BBC nature doc filmmakers are deliberately keeping imperfect footage in the age of AI.
Earlier series were famous for flawless crystal-clear shots that almost felt too good to be real.
Hyper-polished and seamless visuals have now become a dead giveaway of synthetic footage.
By keeping less-than-perfect moments in the edit, the team aims to show the footage is genuine.

article.author: Stevie Bonifield

post.caption:
Switching between AI chats and productivity apps might finally be a thing of the past.

Google Gemini now lets users generate, preview, and edit files directly within the chat interface. Instead of exporting text into separate apps, you can manipulate documents right where you prompted them.

The update includes support for Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, code, and PDFs. The capability starts rolling out today to all Gemini users, with PDF previews and edits supported across both web and mobile.

Will native document editing inside AI chatbots change how you handle daily work?
